claims.text: A thin, adherent Al2O3 interlayer between zirconium alloy and elemental Cr will reduce high-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The Al2O3 interlayer will not compromise oxidation protection under normal operating conditions.
The Al2O3 interlayer will not compromise oxidation protection under accident conditions.
The Al2O3 layer acts as a physical diffusion barrier limiting interfacial element transport.
The Al2O3 layer acts as a chemical diffusion barrier limiting interfacial element transport.
Al2O3 provides an inert interface that inhibits Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Inhibiting Cr–Zr interdiffusion prevents formation of deleterious Cr–Zr intermetallic phases at elevated temperatures.
The interlayer allows the Cr coating to retain its protective oxidation properties.
Relative to Cr-coated zirconium alloy without the interlayer, the modified coating will exhibit reduced interfacial diffusion.
Relative to the unmodified baseline, the modified coating will exhibit improved coating integrity.
Relative to the unmodified baseline, the modified coating will maintain oxidation resistance under both normal and accident conditions.
Elemental Cr-coated zirconium-alloy cladding undergoes premature coating failure because of elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The Al2O3-interlayer coating is expected to be effective during extended exposure near 300°C.
The Al2O3-interlayer coating is expected to be effective in steam up to approximately 1200°C for relatively short accident exposures.
